transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you. Well, what brings me in today is this... constant restless feeling I've been having. It's like I’m just wound too tight and I can’t ever fully settle down. It happens even when I’m supposed to be doing something calm, you know? Like sitting through a long planning meeting for work, or even just on my own time when I'm trying to paint or do yoga. I just can't seem to relax and sit still.
How long have you been experiencing this constant restless, wound-up feeling—days, weeks, or longer?

Oh, definitely longer than days or weeks. I'd say... it's been noticeably harder to manage for about two years and two months now. That was right around the time when some conflicts with my in-laws started taking over a lot of our evenings, and I just haven't really been able to settle down since.
Have you noticed any physical changes along with this restlessness—such as unexplained weight loss, feeling unusually hot or sweaty, a racing heart, or trembling hands?

No, I haven't noticed any of that. My weight has been pretty steady, and I don't feel unusually hot or sweaty. My heart isn't racing, and my hands don't shake. It's really just that internal feeling of being wound up and not being able to sit still.
Over these past two years, have you also noticed a persistent low or depressed mood most of the time, even on days when the restlessness isn't as bad?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, sure, the stuff with my in-laws can be frustrating, but I wouldn't say I feel depressed or down most of the time. My mood is actually pretty normal, I think. It's really just that constant need to be moving or doing something that's the issue.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a number of different things—like work, family, health, or finances—and having a hard time controlling that worry?

No, I wouldn't say I worry excessively. I mean, I have normal everyday stress with work and family, but I don't sit around worrying about my health or finances or anything like that. It's not like my mind is spinning out of control with anxious thoughts. It really is just that physical feeling of needing to keep moving, not a mental worry.
Have you noticed any muscle tension, trouble falling or staying asleep, or increased irritability along with this restless feeling?

No, not really. I mean, my muscles don't feel tense, and I usually sleep just fine once I actually get into bed. As for being irritable... maybe a little bit when I'm forced to sit still for too long, but nothing out of the ordinary. It's really just the physical restlessness itself.
Are you currently taking any medications, particularly antipsychotics, antidepressants, or other prescription drugs?
No, I'm not taking any medications at all right now. No prescriptions, no antidepressants, nothing like that.
Going back to your childhood or teenage years, did you often have trouble paying attention, staying focused on tasks, or sitting still in class?

Yes, actually. I remember... well, in elementary school, I would get notes sent home to my parents pretty often. It was usually because I kept popping out of my seat during class. I also had a habit of talking over my classmates, and I'd always rush to answer things before the teacher even finished asking the question. So, sitting still and waiting my turn was definitely an issue for me back then.
Do you currently have trouble staying focused on tasks, following through on details, or find yourself frequently forgetful or disorganized in daily life?

Well, regarding the details... yes, I've noticed that at work. I'm a buyer, and over the past couple of years, I’ll think I’ve checked a vendor spreadsheet completely and carefully. But then our planning coordinator will catch something—like I transposed a SKU, or I missed a freight surcharge. Sometimes I've even carried the wrong quantity over into the purchase order. So, I do make those kinds of mistakes, even when I feel like I was paying attention.

Between your school years and now, did these attention and restlessness difficulties continue fairly consistently, or was there a period in your teens or twenties where they mostly went away before coming back?

I'm not really sure, honestly. I haven't exactly tracked it over the years. I mean... I don't remember a specific time in my twenties or thirties where everything just completely went away. I think it's just sort of how I've always been. But I didn't really pay close attention to it back then, so I can't say for certain if there was a gap or if it's just been a constant thing in the background.
